acceptance_reason: Vessel keeps one semantic identity and unchanged local hull state; exactly one current owner exists; world placement changes coherently; old-region work cannot mutate the post-crossing vessel.

definition.fail_criteria: Crossing rewrites local hull identity, duplicates/removes hull state, creates overlapping/no ownership, or allows stale old-region commits.
definition.inconclusive_conditions: Fixture teleports a static mesh/object without exercising editable vessel-local state or ownership transfer.
invalidation_conditions: Evidence is unusable due to wrong build/configuration, measurement defect or contamination.
A proof run without adequate exact build identity may be INVALIDATED.
definition.pass_criteria: Vessel keeps one semantic identity and unchanged local hull state; exactly one current owner exists; world placement changes coherently; old-region work cannot mutate the post-crossing vessel.
procedure: Cross an editable vessel containing hull, cargo, state and an occupant over explicit region boundaries.
Delay owner transfer and release old-region work after crossing.
Reverse direction and cross with pending hull/collision work.
definition.question: Can an editable vessel cross world/region/partition boundaries without rewriting vessel-local identity, duplicating hull state or losing authoritative ownership?
definition.required_repetition: At least 5,000 crossings across direction, speed, size and pending-work cases.
definition.title: Vessel Region Crossing

observations: Region crossing changed placement ownership epochs while preserving vessel-local identity and hull state.
